drivingQuestion: May one recite the havdala blessing over fire seen outside a town whose population is half gentile and half Jewish?
outcomeNote: The contradiction is dissolved: the seifa's wording is stylistic, and a half-and-half town permits the blessing.

segments.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָיָה מְהַלֵּךְ חוּץ לַכְּרַךְ וְרָאָה אוּר, אִם רוֹב גּוֹיִם — אֵינוֹ מְבָרֵךְ, אִם רוֹב יִשְׂרָאֵל — מְבָרֵךְ.
segments.en: «The Sages taught» in a baraita: «If one was walking outside the city, saw fire» there, and wanted to recite the blessing over it as part of havdala, «if» the city has a «majority of gentiles he may not recite the blessing» over the fire, but «if» the city has a «majority of Jews, he may recite the blessing.»

segments.he: הָא גוּפָא קַשְׁיָא, אָמְרַתְּ אִם רוֹב גּוֹיִם — אֵינוֹ מְבָרֵךְ, הָא מֶחֱצָה עַל מֶחֱצָה — מְבָרֵךְ, וַהֲדַר תָּנֵי אִם רוֹב יִשְׂרָאֵל — מְבָרֵךְ, הָא מֶחֱצָה עַל מֶחֱצָה — אֵינוֹ מְבָרֵךְ!
segments.en: The Gemara notes: «The matter itself is difficult» in this baraita. «You said» in the baraita that if the town has a «majority of gentiles he may not recite the blessing.» By inference, if the town population was «half» gentiles «and half» Jews, «one may recite a blessing. And then you teach» that «if» the town has a «majority of Jews, he may recite the blessing.» By inference, if the town population was «half» gentiles «and half» Jews, «one may not recite a blessing.» The inferences from two sections of the baraita are contradictory.

segments.he: בְּדִין הוּא דַּאֲפִילּוּ מֶחֱצָה עַל מֶחֱצָה נָמֵי מְבָרֵךְ, וְאַיְּידִי דִּתְנָא רֵישָׁא ״רוֹב נׇכְרִים״, תְּנָא סֵיפָא ״רוֹב יִשְׂרָאֵל״.
segments.en: The Gemara responds: «By right,» the baraita should have taught that «even» if the town population was «half» gentiles «and half» Jews, «one may recite a blessing,» but «since in the first clause it taught: The majority of gentiles, in the latter clause it» used the same expression and «taught: The majority of Jews.»

moves.summary: The baraita: one who sees fire outside a town blesses over it only if the town's majority is Jewish
